content: Caduet is a medication that combines two active ingredients: amlodipine, a calcium channel blocker, and atorvastatin, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor. It is prescribed to treat patients with both high cholesterol and high blood pressure or chest pain. Amlodipine works by relaxing and widening blood vessels, which helps reduce chest pain and lower blood pressure. Atorvastatin lowers the risk of heart attack and chest pain by reducing levels of bad cholesterol (e.g., triglycerides) and increasing good cholesterol (e.g., high-density lipoprotein) in the blood. Do NOT use Caduet if: You are allergic to any of its ingredients. You have active liver disease or persistently elevated liver enzyme levels of unknown cause. You are taking itraconazole, mibefradil, or an HIV protease inhibitor (e.g., indinavir). You are pregnant or breastfeeding. If any of these conditions apply to you, contact your doctor or healthcare provider immediately. Before using Caduet: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any of the following conditions: Pregnancy, plans to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Use of any prescription or nonprescription medications, herbal preparations, or dietary supplements. Allergies to medicines, foods, or other substances. Severe infections, blood infections, or severe endocrine, metabolic, or electrolyte disorders, or if you are very ill. Low blood pressure, heart problems, or a history of heart failure, liver problems, diabetes, thyroid problems, kidney problems, muscle problems, stroke, or uncontrolled seizures. Recent surgery or a serious injury. Consumption of three or more alcoholic drinks per day. Drug Interactions: Caduet may interact with other medications. Inform your healthcare provider if you are taking any of the following: Amiodarone, cyclosporine, diltiazem, fibrates (e.g., gemfibrozil), fluconazole, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., indinavir), HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g., simvastatin), imatinib, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ketolide antibiotics (e.g., telithromycin), macrolide antibiotics (e.g., erythromycin), mibefradil, nefazodone, niacin, streptogramins (e.g., dalfopristin), verapamil, or voriconazole, as these may increase the risk of severe muscle problems. Sildenafil, as it may increase the risk of low blood pressure. Vasopressin receptor antagonists (e.g., conivaptan), as they may increase the risk of amlodipine's side effects. Digoxin or oral contraceptives (e.g., norethindrone/estradiol), as Caduet may increase the risk of their side effects. Bosentan, carbamazepine, efavirenz, rifampin, or St. John’s wort, as these may decrease Caduet's effectiveness. This is not a complete list of possible interactions. Consult your healthcare provider for more information. How to use Caduet: Take Caduet exactly as directed by your doctor. Follow the dosing instructions on the label. It can be taken with or without food. Take Caduet at least one hour before or four to six hours after taking cholestyramine. Use Caduet on a regular schedule to maximize its benefits. Taking it at the same time each day will help you remember. Avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while taking Caduet, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Consult your doctor before including grapefruit in your diet. Continue using Caduet even if you feel well, as high blood pressure and high cholesterol often do not cause symptoms. Do not miss any doses. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as possible. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once. If you miss more than one dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist. Important Safety Information: Caduet may cause drowsiness or dizziness, which can be worsened by alcohol or certain medications. Use caution when driving or performing tasks that require alertness until you know how the medication affects you. If you consume more than three alcoholic drinks per day, discuss this with your doctor before taking Caduet. Follow the diet, exercise, and weight reduction program recommended by your healthcare provider. Maintain proper dental hygiene while taking Caduet. Brush and floss regularly, and visit your dentist as advised. Inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking Caduet before undergoing any medical or dental procedures, emergency care, or surgery. It may take several weeks for Caduet to show its full effects. Do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Avoid using over-the-counter cough-and-cold products or diet aids without consulting your doctor, as they may contain ingredients that could increase your heart rate or blood pressure. If you are taking Caduet for chest pain, note that it will not relieve the pain of a sudden attack. It is intended to prevent or reduce the frequency of chest pain attacks when taken regularly. Have your blood pressure checked regularly while on Caduet. Caduet may rarely cause muscle damage, especially when starting the medication or increasing the dose. This risk is higher when taken with certain other medications. Untreated, this can lead to a serious condition called rhabdomyolysis and kidney damage. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially if accompanied by fever or unusual tiredness. Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control while taking Caduet, as it may harm the fetus. If you suspect pregnancy, contact your doctor immediately. Routine lab tests, including liver and kidney function, blood pressure, and cholesterol levels, may be performed to monitor your condition and check for side effects. Keep all doctor and lab appointments. Use Caduet with caution in elderly patients, as they may be more sensitive to its effects. Caduet is not recommended for use in children, as its safety and effectiveness have not been established. Do not use Caduet if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking it. If you suspect pregnancy, contact your doctor immediately. One of the ingredients in Caduet is found in breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended while on this medication. Possible Side Effects: All medications can cause side effects, but many people experience no or minor side effects. Contact your doctor if any of the following common side effects persist or become bothersome: Constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, drowsiness, flushing, gas, headache, nausea, stomach upset or pain, tiredness, or weakness. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of the following severe side effects: Severe allergic reactions (rash, hives, itching, difficulty breathing, chest tightness, swelling of the mouth, face, lips, or tongue). Changes in urine output, vision changes, dark urine, fainting, fast or irregular heartbeat, increased frequency or severity of chest pain, joint pain, muscle aches or weakness (especially with fever or unusual tiredness), numbness in an arm or leg, pale stools, severe stomach pain, sharp or crushing chest pain, sudden leg pain, sudden severe headache, vomiting, dizziness, fainting, shortness of breath, swelling of the feet or legs, tender or bleeding gums, unexplained weight gain, or yellowing of the eyes or skin. This is not a complete list of side effects. If you have questions or need medical advice, contact your doctor or healthcare provider. Proper Storage: Store Caduet at 77°F (25°C) in a tightly closed container. Brief storage at temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C) is permitted. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep Caduet out of reach of children and pets. General Information: If you have any questions about Caduet, consult your doctor, pharmacist, or healthcare provider. Use Caduet only as prescribed for you. Do not share it with others. If your symptoms do not improve or worsen, contact your doctor.
